You are reviewing the vsim/Verilator side of a hybrid RISC-V co-simulator. Look for **potential bugs** (not improvements, not style nits) in the C++ orchestration that resumes hart state via Debug Module DMI, executes the ROI, drains state, and ships it to QEMU2.

## Scope (only these files; do NOT review the QEMU plugin or shell scripts)

- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/state_loader.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/resume_from_qemu.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/abstract_command.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/measure_start_snapshot.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/systemc_dmi_bus.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/kanata_roi.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/hybrid/exit_codes.hpp
- /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/include/hybrid/state_abi.h  (reference)

## What "working features" means here

CSR mode + PC mode + icount mode + SimPoint mode all currently pass e2e. Look for bugs along those paths.

## Exclude these known limitations (do NOT flag)

- vsim phase assumed trap-free + PMP-static (CSR restore split; ResumeDriver only writes mstatus/mtvec/mcycle/minstret)
- Little-endian only (RV64 + x86_64 host)
- HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64 (VLEN up to 512 bits)
- Phase-2 ROI cannot issue syscalls
- Header-only orchestration layer (intentional)
- Any limitation explicitly called out in /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/CLAUDE.md

## Pay special attention to (per CLAUDE.md, these were subtle)

- Restore order: mstatus.VS -> V data sweep -> vsetvl (vl in x5, vtype in x6) -> vstart AFTER vsetvl -> vxsat/vxrm/vcsr -> GPRs
- V data sweep clobbers x5/x6/x7 -- ensure GPRs are restored AFTER, not before
- Drain order: V dump sweep must run LAST so its vsetvl clobbers and counter increments don't corrupt drained state
- mcycle/minstret freeze/unfreeze around drain
- Scratch region stride is HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX (compile-time), not runtime vlenb

## What to look for (concrete bug categories)

- DMI sequence errors: write before halt, busy-bit not polled, abstract command issued without checking cmderr
- Program Buffer corruption: register clobber that races with the architectural restore
- vsetvl semantics: forgetting that vsetvl resets vstart, that vtype write requires the vsetvl form
- mcycle/minstret accounting: counter delta wrong if hart did extra instructions during halt-resume bookkeeping; uses 64-bit reads on RV64
- mstatus.VS / FS field-extract bugs (wrong bit positions, wrong mask)
- VLEN mismatch between binary and runtime config (32-byte runtime vs 64-byte wire)
- Race between trigger detection and DMI halt (e.g., detect CSR exit, but hart retires one more insn before halt)
- Off-by-one in icount window (counted at retire vs commit; first-instruction inclusion semantics)
- Endian / hex / byte-order issues writing P-packets or DMI words
- Lifetime/aliasing bugs in C++: dangling refs, copies vs moves of large state structs
- Error paths that silently swallow failures and proceed with stale state
- gdbstub-restore path that runs even on partial drain (corrupting QEMU2)
- kanata ROI logging that doesn't pair cleanly with phase boundaries

## Output format (strict)

For each bug, write a single bullet:

`<severity> | <file>:<line> | <one-sentence description> | <why this is wrong>`

Severities: CRITICAL (round-trip breaks, silent state corruption), HIGH (wrong cycle count or wrong end state on plausible workloads), MEDIUM (edge cases), LOW (latent / unreachable today).

Cap the whole report at 25 bullets. Don't propose fixes. Don't restate architecture. Don't flag the same bug across multiple files -- pick the canonical site.

1	// V-register transport staging: the host<->guest-RAM half of the V data
2	// regfile transfer. The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for
3	// v0..v31 (the RISC-V Debug Spec leaves V to the Program Buffer or
4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see
6	// pb_v_data_sweep in program_buffer.hpp, driven by ResumeDriver on resume and
7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores a fixed scratch region of
8	// guest RAM (kVScratchGpa); this header provides the matching host-side copy:
9	//
10	//   - stage_v_to_scratch: state.vreg[] -> scratch RAM, called before resume so
11	//     the ResumeDriver vle8.v sweep reads QEMU 1's V values.
12	//   - read_v_from_scratch: scratch RAM -> state.vreg[], called after the
13	//     StateDrain vse8.v sweep so qemu_handback can ship v0..v31 to QEMU 2 via
14	//     the gdbstub P packets.
15	//
16	// The transfer is transparent to the workload: benchmark binaries issue no
17	// transport code, only the enter_vsim / exit_vsim markers. rt_c_v_regs.c is
18	// the reference fixture.
19	//
20	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus. Easy to unit-test.
21	
22	#pragma once
23	
24	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
25	
26	#include <cstddef>
27	#include <cstdint>
28	#include <cstring>
29	#include <span>
30	#include <stdexcept>
31	
32	namespace hybrid
33	{
34	
35	// Reserved scratch slot inside the shared mmap. Sits well above the C
36	// runtime's _stack (rt_c.ld places it at RAM_BASE + 0x700000), giving the
37	// stack ~9 MiB of headroom before colliding with this 2 KiB region. On
38	// `-M andes_ae350` RAM is at 0x00000000 and the GPA is 0x00FF0000; on
39	// `-M virt` it would be 0x80FF0000. ResumeDriver/StateDrain stage the PB
40	// sweep's base pointer (x7) directly from this constant, so it is the single
41	// source of truth -- no fixture-side literal to keep in sync.
42	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000ull;
43	
44	// Total scratch bytes needed: 32 V regs × HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX. Sized to
45	// the maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`.
46	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes =
47	  static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX;
48	
49	namespace detail
50	{
51	
52	// Translate scratch GPA into a byte offset inside a RAM span whose first
53	// byte sits at `ram_base`. Throws if the scratch region falls outside the
54	// supplied span (i.e. the caller passed a too-small RAM mapping).
55	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size, uint64_t ram_base)
56	  -> std::size_t
57	{
58	  if (kVScratchGpa < ram_base)
59	    throw std::runtime_error(
60	      "v_regfile_xfer: scratch GPA below RAM base");
61	  const auto off = static_cast<std::size_t>(kVScratchGpa - ram_base);
62	  if (off + kVScratchBytes > ram_size)
63	    throw std::runtime_error(
64	      "v_regfile_xfer: scratch region exceeds RAM span");
65	  return off;
66	}
67	
68	}  // namespace detail
69	
70	// Copy state.vreg[] into ram[scratch_offset .. scratch_offset+kVScratchBytes].
71	// Called just before vsim resumes the hart so the fixture can vle8.v from
72	// scratch and pick up QEMU 1's V values.
73	inline void stage_v_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
74	                               std::span<uint8_t> ram,
75	                               uint64_t ram_base)
76	{
77	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size(), ram_base);
78	  std::memcpy(ram.data() + off, state.vreg, kVScratchBytes);
79	}
80	
81	// Copy ram[scratch_offset .. +kVScratchBytes] into state.vreg[]. Called
82	// inside the vsim drain path after the fixture's prologue vse8.v has
83	// settled the (possibly mutated) regfile bytes into RAM.
84	inline void read_v_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
85	                                std::span<const uint8_t> ram,
86	                                uint64_t ram_base)
87	{
88	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size(), ram_base);
89	  std::memcpy(state.vreg, ram.data() + off, kVScratchBytes);
90	}
91	
92	}  // namespace hybrid
93

1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <array>
17	#include <cstdint>
18	#include <span>
19	#include <stdexcept>
20	#include <string>
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
25	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
26	
27	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
28	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
29	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
30	
31	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
32	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
33	
34	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
35	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
36	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
37	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
38	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
39	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
40	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
41	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
42	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
43	
44	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
45	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
46	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
47	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
48	{
49	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
50	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
52	         | (0b111u << 12)
53	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
54	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
55	}
56	
57	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
58	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
59	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
60	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
61	{
62	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
63	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
64	         | (0b001u << 12)
65	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
66	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
67	}
68	
69	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
70	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
71	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
72	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
73	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
74	{
75	    return (1u << 25)
76	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
77	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
78	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
79	}
80	
81	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
82	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
83	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
84	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
85	{
86	    return (1u << 25)
87	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
88	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
89	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
90	}
91	
92	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
93	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
94	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then returns whether cmderr stayed clear.
95	//
96	// Returns true on success; false if the DM set cmderr during execution.
97	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns or poll
98	// times out.
99	template<typename Bus>
100	inline bool exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
101	{
102	    constexpr uint8_t  kAbstractcs   = 0x16u;
103	    constexpr uint8_t  kCommand      = 0x17u;
104	    constexpr uint32_t kBusy         = 1u << 12;
105	    constexpr uint32_t kCmderrMask   = 0x7u << 8;
106	
107	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
108	        throw std::runtime_error(
109	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
110	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
111	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
112	
113	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
114	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
115	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
116	
117	    if ((bus.read(kAbstractcs) & kCmderrMask) != 0u)
118	        bus.write(kAbstractcs, kCmderrMask);
119	
120	    bus.write(kCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
121	    poll_until_clear(bus, kAbstractcs, kBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
122	
123	    return (bus.read(kAbstractcs) & kCmderrMask) == 0u;
124	}
125	
126	// vtype encoding for e8, m1, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=000, vta=1, vma=1).
127	// The V-data sweep loads/stores one byte-element per lane (vl=vlenb).
128	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M1 = 0xC0u;
129	
130	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
131	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
132	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
133	template<typename Bus>
134	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
135	{
136	    constexpr uint8_t  kData0      = 0x04u;
137	    constexpr uint8_t  kData1      = 0x05u;
138	    constexpr uint8_t  kAbstractcs = 0x16u;
139	    constexpr uint8_t  kCommand    = 0x17u;
140	    constexpr uint32_t kBusy       = 1u << 12;
141	    bus.write(kData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
142	    bus.write(kData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
143	    bus.write(kCommand,
144	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
145	    poll_until_clear(bus, kAbstractcs, kBusy, "write_register_abstract");
146	}
147	
148	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and a contiguous
149	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
150	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
151	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m1 sets vl=vlenb (one
152	// byte-element per lane) and forces vstart=0, so each unit-stride access
153	// covers the whole register even when the hart had vstart!=0. Uses x5/x6
154	// (vsetvl operands) and x7 (base pointer) as scratch. `stride` is the
155	// per-register byte spacing in the scratch region (the wire format reserves
156	// HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX per reg, independent of the runtime vlenb).
157	template<typename Bus>
158	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t stride,
159	                            uint64_t vlenb, bool load)
160	{
161	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(5), vlenb);       // AVL
162	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(6), kVtypeE8M1);  // e8, m1, ta, ma
163	    const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb_vsetvl = { encode_vsetvl(0, 5, 6) };
164	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb_vsetvl});
165	    for (uint16_t i = 0; i < 32; ++i) {
166	        write_register_abstract(
167	            bus, regno_gpr(7), scratch_gpa + static_cast<uint64_t>(i) * stride);
168	        const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb = {
169	            load ? encode_vle8_v(static_cast<uint8_t>(i), 7)
170	                 : encode_vse8_v(static_cast<uint8_t>(i), 7) };
171	        exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb});
172	    }
173	}
174	
175	}  // namespace hybrid
176

1	// IcountTrigger - F6 sibling of CsrTrigger. Counts retired insns and fires
2	// HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT once the per-hart counter reaches the configured target.
3	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus.
4	//
5	// Duck-types the CsrTrigger surface so HandoffController's template
6	// instantiates cleanly for either:
7	//
8	//   - lookup(pc) -> std::optional<CsrTriggerHit>
9	//   - empty() -> bool
10	//   - observe_commit() -> void  (icount-specific; HandoffController calls
11	//                                via if-constexpr requires-clause)
12	//
13	// `pc` is ignored: icount fires on counter alone, not at any specific PC.

content.content:
1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.
5	
6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a three-phase round-trip: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain) -> **QEMU2** (restore via gdbstub, continue).
9	
10	Two Git submodules:
11	- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
12	- `verilator/` - vsim sources; `hybrid/` subdirs hold the plugin and test fixtures
13	- `tools/simpoint/` - SimPoint 3.2 (UCSD) clustering binary; pinned to upstream `17783e5`
14	
15	Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).
16	
17	## Build Commands
18	
19	**Primary path (`./hsim`)** -- the end-user driver, used in all user-facing docs:
20	
21	```sh
22	./hsim build                       # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
23	./hsim test                        # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
24	./hsim run <elf> --mode csr|pc|icount|slice  # one round-trip
25	./hsim list <fixtures|modes>
26	```
27	
28	**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
29	working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:
30	
31	```sh
32	# Build everything (qemu -> vsim -> plugin -> simpoint)
33	source ./setup.sh
34	
35	# Build individual components
36	./scripts/build_qemu.sh                              # QEMU (configure + make -j64)
37	./scripts/build_vsim.sh                              # vsim (Docker/podman, runs ./build.sh inside container)
38	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=./QEMU  # TCG plugin (out-of-tree)
39	./scripts/build_simpoint.sh                          # SimPoint clustering binary (g++ on host)
40	
41	# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
42	make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
43	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture
44	
45	# Clean
46	source ./setup.sh clean [qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|all]
47	```
48	
49	**Outputs:**
50	- `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`
51	- `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium` (or other CPU variant)
52	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`
53	- `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`
54	
55	`scripts/build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman). It builds an image from `verilator/Dockerfile` (target `env`) then runs `./build.sh` inside it, mounting the repo at `/work` and `include/` as `/include:ro`.
56	
57	## Running Tests
58	
59	```sh
60	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
61	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
62	
63	# Run with specific options
64	JOBS=4 MODE=csr bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, CSR-mode only
65	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
66	FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
67	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
68	
69	# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
70	# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
71	# To run ctest directly after build:
72	#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
73	```
74	
75	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
76	
77	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
78	
79	**Manual driver tests**: `tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh` are per-feature RED-then-green smoke tests for `./hsim` subcommands (F1..F14). They are run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).
80	
81	## Architecture
82	
83	### Three-Phase Handoff
84	
85	```
86	QEMU1 --(state file)--> vsim --(state file + V-scratch mmap)--> QEMU2
87	```
88	
89	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On CSR-write trigger (`csrwi 0x7C0, 0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
90	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
91	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
92	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands.
93	5. **qemu_handback** (`src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`) - Spawns QEMU2, connects via gdbstub, sends P-packet register writes for GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-regs, then `continue`s.
94	
95	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are restored only on QEMU2 via the gdbstub P-packet path in `qemu_handback`. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
96	
97	### Trigger Modes
98	
99	The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile.
100	
101	Kernel modes (measure one region you choose):
102	- **CSR mode** (default): Pattern-matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (entry) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) at retire time. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes ax45mp.
103	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; CSR insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
104	
105	Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count):
106	- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for CSR-less workloads.
107	- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim estimate`). The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.
108	
109	`./hsim run --mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint` is the unified orchestrator; `tests/e2e.sh` drives csr/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.
110	
111	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
112	
113	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the handback path. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` supports VLEN up to 512 bits. Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
114	
115	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`.
116	
117	### V-State Transport
118	
119	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a fixed scratch region
120	(`kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` on `-M andes_ae350`) in the shared mmap. vsim drives
121	the transfer via the Debug Module **Program Buffer** while the hart is halted, so
122	benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
123	- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
124	  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
125	  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
126	- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
127	  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
128	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]`.
129	- `qemu_handback` ships them to QEMU2 via gdbstub P-packets by register number.
130	
131	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m1 (vl=vlenb), which also forces vstart=0 so
132	the unit-stride access covers the whole register. The scratch stride is the
133	compile-time `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` (wire-format per-register span), not the
134	runtime vlenb.
135	
136	V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
137	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
138	- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)
139	
140	Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
141	1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
142	2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m1 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
143	   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
144	   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
145	3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
146	4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
147	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
148	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
149	
150	`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
151	LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
152	sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.
153	
154	### Test Fixtures
155	
156	All fixtures run on the unified `tests/hybrid/e2e.sh` harness, which
157	sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
158	the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 round-trip. Two fixture families:
159	
160	| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
161	|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
162	| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
163	| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | linked against vsim-demo C runtime. Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- the stack/heap and `main()`'s ra-spill/restore around `csrwi 0x7C0,1` must survive vsim -> QEMU2. |
164	
165	The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
166	then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.
167	
168	Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`. C-level fixtures link `runtime/{crt0.S, trap.S, handler.c}` plus the Andes toolchain's `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting-backed libgloss), using `rt_c.ld`. V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. **Phase-2 rule:** the span between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()` runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall (no `printf`, `fopen`, semihosting ebreak, etc.) -- vsim does not implement semihosting, so any libgloss-routed call inside the ROI traps. Phase 1 and phase 3 print via standard newlib stdio (both QEMUs are launched with `-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`).
169	
170	### vsim CMake Structure
171	
172	vsim lives entirely in `verilator/`. Key CMake options:
173	- `VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID` (default OFF) - enables e2e CTest registration
174	- `VSIM_CONFIG_FILE` - CPU YAML (default `config.yaml`)
175	- `VSIM_NO_VERILATOR` - skip Verilator build (assume prebuilt)
176	
177	The hybrid orchestration layer (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`) is header-only and depends only on C++20 standard library + the shared ABI header. SystemC/Verilator are not required for hybrid unit tests.
178	
179	Hybrid unit tests (`tests/hybrid/`) use [doctest](https://github.com/doctest/doctest). They are registered in `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` and run via `ctest`. The `recording_bus.hpp` / `RecordingSession` patterns provide duck-typed test doubles for the DMI bus and gdbstub session without requiring virtual interfaces.
180	
181	## Key Files
182	
183	| File | Purpose |
184	|------|---------|
185	| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
186	| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
187	| `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` | Phase dispatcher |
188	| `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | DMI state restore (Tier A+B) |
189	| `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | DMI state capture |
190	| `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` | Spawn QEMU2, gdbstub P-packets |
191	| `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` | V register transport via scratch region |
192	| `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` | CTest registration for all e2e fixtures |
193	| `scripts/run_e2e.sh` | Parallel e2e runner (FIFO job pool, per-test logs) |
194	| `tests/fixtures/Makefile` | RISC-V ELF fixture build (Andes toolchain) |

Based on my comprehensive analysis of the code, here are the bugs I found:

**CRITICAL | verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:109,167 | exec_progbuf() return value silently ignored; Program Buffer execution errors proceed without notification | If a Program Buffer instruction fails (cmderr set during vsetvl or vle8.v), the function returns false but callers don't check, leaving V registers partially restored and vstart/vtype/vl in inconsistent states, corrupting subsequent V operations.**

**CRITICAL | verilator/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:171 | exec_progbuf() return value ignored in pb_v_data_sweep loop; fails silently on vector register load/store errors | If vle8.v or vse8.v fails for any v0..v31 register, the sweep continues and silently skips that register, causing data corruption when drained back to QEMU2.**
